newsitem.title: USA: AFLAC Inc says yen translation hurt Q1.
newsitem.headline: AFLAC Inc says yen translation hurt Q1.

text.p: AFLAC Inc said Tuesday the translation of yen into dollars reduced operating earnings by $0.06 per share during the first quarter and new business in Japan declined during the quarter.
The insurance holding company expects sales in Japan to improve as the year progresses.

"Most importantly, AFLAC Japan continued to achieve its earnings objectives. With our leadership positions in the United States and Japan -- the two best insurance markets in the world -- we expect our strong performance excluding the effect of the yen to continue," said Daniel Amos, president and chief executive.

AFLAC posted first-quarter operating earnings of $90.5 million, or $0.64 per share, compared with $86.9 million, or $0.59 per share, a year ago. Total revenues for the first quarter were $1.7 billion.
